identity.title: Representation Entanglement for Generation: Training Diffusion Transformers Is Much Easier Than You Think

problem.claim: Diffusion models face training challenges that external visual-representation alignment can mitigate.

gap.claim: Because external alignment is absent throughout denoising inference, it may not fully exploit discriminative representations.

contributions.claim: Proposes REG, which entangles low-level image latents with one high-level pretrained class token during denoising.
Frames inference as concurrent reconstruction of image latents and global semantics, with semantic knowledge guiding generation.
Adds one denoising token with reported overhead below 0.5% in FLOPs and latency.

stated_novelty.claim: REG integrates a single high-level class token with low-level image latents for denoising, extending the role of pretrained representations beyond external alignment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SiT-XL/2 + REG on ImageNet 256×256 trains 63× faster than SiT-XL/2 and 23× faster than SiT-XL/2 + REPA.
The authors report that SiT-L/2 + REG trained for 400K iterations outperforms SiT-XL/2 + REPA trained for 4M iterations.
The authors report improved generation quality and training efficiency, with negligible additional inference overhead.

narrative_sequence.summary: External visual representations and noisy-to-clean alignment are described as effective for mitigating diffusion training challenges.
The abstract argues that alignment unavailable during inference underuses discriminative representations.
REG entangles image latents with a single pretrained high-level class token during denoising.
The process reconstructs image content and global semantics together, adding less than 0.5% FLOPs and latency.
On ImageNet, REG is reported to accelerate convergence substantially and to outperform a larger, longer-trained REPA baseline.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a stated inference-time limitation directly to a method that makes semantics part of the denoising process, then reports both efficiency and quality outcomes.

lessons.interpretation: A compact problem–mechanism–outcome chain can make a representation-learning proposal easier to assess.
lessons.application: When presenting a training intervention, explicitly map the diagnosed missing signal to where the model uses it, then report outcomes under named baselines and budgets.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the mechanism-to-outcome link is only speculative or when comparable training budgets are unavailable.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide absolute quality metrics, convergence criteria, datasets beyond the stated ImageNet setting, or statistical variation.
The meanings of “outperforms,” “63× faster,” and “23× faster” and the hardware or measurement conditions are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish independent verification, reproducibility, or priority of the stated novelty.
